clue.text: Married without honour, wife leaves to get hammered?

indicators.note: whatever leaves is no longer present, so that letter is taken out
'without' in its old sense of 'outside', so one word wraps around another

parts.note: married is a synonym of wedded
an MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A disgraced husband whose wife walks out turns to drink and gets thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The honour slots in after the first letter of the marriage word, and only then does the wife's letter drop out. 'Hammered' looks like slang for drunk, but the question mark points to a nail driven firmly in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hammered in has been driven deep and fixed firmly within its surroundings, which is a punning description of being set solidly inside.

clue.text: Domain of politician in Ireland

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the constituency or territory of an Irish politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire is the Irish-language name for the Republic of Ireland, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a sovereign's realm or territory, the lands ruled over, which is what a domain means.

clue.text: Singer in a stag party goes first

indicators.note: an item that goes first is placed at the front, ahead of the rest of the build

parts.note: a ball is a formal dancing party
taken as written
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A crooner turns up to perform at a raucous stag party before the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag party' reads as one phrase (a bachelor party), but the words split: the stag is a deer and the party is a dance, which moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a performer of ballads, sentimental or narrative songs, so a vocalist or crooner.

clue.text: Embarrassed about recently cleared out city

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

indicators.note: a word cleared out has had its inside emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of 'recently'

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed that a city has recently been evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: Derry, also called Londonderry, is a city in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Derry is a major urban centre in Northern Ireland, so it is one example of a city.

clue.text: Finally persuade Roman governor to remove hair

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of 'persuade'
Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judaea

explanation.surface: Someone at last talks a Roman official into a spot of grooming.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman governor is the one from the Gospels, who presided over the trial of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: To epilate is to strip unwanted body growth out by the roots, as with waxing or an electric device.

clue.text: Sample of zinc has tested 'pure'

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from something larger, so the letters are found inside the text

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: A laboratory reports that a zinc sample has been assayed and found pure.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are concealed across zin(C HAS TE)sted; the quotation marks make 'pure' look like a lab result.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually virtuous and abstinent, the moral sense of pure and unsullied.

clue.text: Main ways one enters bars after being intoxicated

indicators.note: coming after means placed later in sequence, so this part follows the other

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: rods are bars of metal
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone staggers into the pubs having already got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs to match 'intoxicated', but it means metal rods.
explanation.definitionFit: High roads are principal routes, the chief thoroughfares between towns, so main ways.

clue.text: Beginning to go mad, upset and hurt

indicators.note: something upset is overturned, so in a down clue the letters are flipped end to end
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'go'
nuts is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone starting to lose their mind is distressed and wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: G and NUTS make GNUTS, which turns over to read STUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stung is to be wounded, either by an insect or by unkind words, so pained or injured.

clue.text: One could be on the way out

definitions.text: One could be on the way out

parts.words: One could be on the way out
parts.note: surface reading: something that is dying or going out of fashion
setter's reading: a notice literally mounted over the route by which people leave a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way out' usually means declining or near death; here it is literal, a sign placed on the route leading out.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a sign is a lit notice fixed above doors and corridors to direct people towards leaving the building.

clue.text: Photograph of famous designer a hack returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous French fashion designer
taken as written
to hack is to chop or lop

explanation.surface: A journalist brings back a picture of a celebrated fashion designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' invites a journalist, which suits the photograph, but it is the verb meaning to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polaroid is an instant print from the camera brand that develops itself, so a kind of snapshot.

clue.text: Condition nursed by fantastic beast

indicators.note: something nursed is held close in the arms, so one piece is cradled inside another

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with I for the 1
gout is a medical condition causing painful joints

explanation.surface: A mythical creature suffers from an ailment that needs nursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic beast' reads as a mythical monster, but 'fantastic' gives A1, with I standing in for the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: An agouti is a burrowing rodent of Central and South America, so a kind of animal or creature.

clue.text: Soup runs regularly provide work

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A charity's regular soup runs provide jobs for volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every other letter of 'Soup runs', starting from the second: O, P, U, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a composition or artistic creation, often a numbered piece of music, so a work.

clue.text: Willing to study finale of play

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of 'play'

explanation.surface: A student is keen to go over the closing scene of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: At British universities you 'read' a subject, meaning you study it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready can mean inclined or prepared to do something, as in 'ready to help', which matches willing.

clue.text: Make sweet rolls to go with a spring vegetable

parts.note: taken as written
a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: something that rolls turns over, so the letters come out backwards

parts.note: to sugar something is to sweeten it

explanation.surface: A baker sweetens bread rolls to serve alongside a springtime vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet rolls' looks like a baked good and 'spring vegetable' like a seasonal crop; in fact 'Make sweet' is SUGAR, 'rolls' turns it round, and the spring is a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a plant whose tender green shoots are eaten cooked, a classic early-season vegetable.

clue.text: Change one's mind about green energy

indicators.note: to turn about is to move around, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A politician performs a U-turn on environmental power policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', but it rearranges the letters of 'green' plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or commitment, so to reverse a decision and back out.

clue.text: Auctioned off the means to acquire knowledge

indicators.note: something off is wrong or not right, so the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A school or library has been sold off at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auctioned off' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, and 'off' tells you to rearrange 'Auctioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling and instruction are how people come to learn things, so education is the route to learning.

clue.text: In this way, a band is flying high

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
taken as written
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A music group is enjoying great success in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is the circular sort worn on a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaring describes rising or gliding at great altitude, as a bird or aircraft does in the sky.

clue.text: Created popular new egg-shaped food at last

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
N is the abbreviation for new
ovate means egg-shaped

indicators.note: what comes at last is at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of 'food'

explanation.surface: A chef finally invents a trendy new dish shaped like an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Ovate is a botanical word for an egg-shaped outline, often used of leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce or devise something new, so innovated means invented or brought into being.

clue.text: One with a fatal vulnerability longs to take sick

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
ill is a synonym of sick

explanation.surface: A frail person yearns to fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Achilles was the Greek hero dipped in the Styx by his heel, which stayed unprotected and was where an arrow killed him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek warrior was invulnerable everywhere except his heel, a single weak point that proved deadly, hence the phrase Achilles heel.

clue.text: By the sound of it, gentleman supplies current pathway

indicators.note: what we judge by its sound is heard rather than read, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: sir is a title for a gentleman, and kit means supplies or equipment

explanation.surface: A gentleman seems to provide the route for an electric flow.
explanation.walkthrough: Say SIR KIT aloud and it matches the spelling C-I-R-C-U-I-T.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical circuit is the closed loop of wires and components through which electricity flows.

clue.text: Darkness arising when there's no good light

indicators.note: something arising goes upwards, so in a down entry the letters read from bottom to top
when something is absent it has been removed, so that letter drops out

parts.note: night is the time of darkness
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Gloom sets in because there is no decent lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGHT loses G to leave NIHT, which then reads upward. 'Light' tempts as the opposite of darkness, but it means slight.
explanation.definitionFit: Light and thin are synonyms for something insubstantial or slender, as with a flimsy fabric or sparse drizzle.

clue.text: Company takes a wrong gamble here

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
taken as written
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A firm makes a bad bet at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A wrong gamble' reads as a misjudged bet; the definition is 'gamble here', describing the place itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people place bets on games of chance like roulette or cards.

clue.text: Fashion scheme — I admitted making garment

indicators.note: someone admitted is let inside, so this letter is placed within the others
to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters are remade into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A designer admits to a plan for making a new item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' poses as the clothing industry, matching 'garment', but it is a verb telling you to reshape the letters of SCHEME with I added.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shift or slip worn as underwear or a simple dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: I invested in capital markets, initially withdrawing personal account

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the letters go back the way they came
money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: what comes initially comes at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'markets'
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor writes about putting money into the financial markets and then pulling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital markets' is a finance phrase, but 'capital' is a city, ROME; add M, reverse to get MEMOR, then put I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A memoir is a written record of the author's own life and experiences, an autobiographical narrative.

clue.text: Unoriginal musical chicken almost making a comeback

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
a comeback is a return to where one started, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón
chicken means timid; almost all of it is kept

explanation.surface: A derivative stage show about a chicken is nearly revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like a bird, but it is the adjective meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitative work copies or mimics something else instead of being new, which is what unoriginal describes.

clue.text: A lot of ladies failing to be perfect

indicators.note: a lot is most but not all, so one letter is dropped from the end
something failing is breaking down, so these letters are put into disorder

parts.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Many women fall short of some standard of perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' reads as falling short, but it is the signal to rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective describes something flawless, exactly as one would wish, so a synonym.

clue.text: Film second contest

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.walkthrough: 'Half a mo' is British for 'just a second', so MO stands for a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie is the everyday American word for a motion picture shown in a cinema.

clue.text: A couple of notes about a US city

indicators.note: about means around, so one pair wraps round the other piece

parts.note: two of the sol-fa note mi
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone jots a few lines about an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests written jottings, but they are musical: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large metropolis in Florida, so one example of an American urban centre.

clue.text: Doesn't get up to misrepresent evil

parts.note: to lie is to misrepresent the truth
a sin is an evil act

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to stand up and give a false account of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break moves: the two pieces join and then divide as four letters plus two.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lies in stays in bed late in the morning, so the phrase means remaining abed.

clue.text: Herb or spice scattered in car lot

indicators.note: things scattered are thrown about in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seasonings have been spilled across a used-car forecourt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the spice in the car lot, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilantro is the American name for coriander, whose leaves serve as a herb and whose seeds as a spice.

clue.text: Special wound dressing gives support

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A particular bandage offers relief and support to an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Lint here is the soft linen dressing for wounds, not fluff.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid strip strapped to a broken limb to hold it steady, a brace.

clue.text: What's left if there isn't a hint?

indicators.note: if something isn't there it has been taken away, so that letter drops out

parts.note: the remainder is what is left over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle: what remains when no clue is given?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left' is REMAINDER; take away the A to get the answer. 'Hint' looks like the thing that is missing, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a prompt that jogs the memory, a nudge or cue, which is what a hint can be.
